damageMappingControls.description: repaint only the pulsing child widget; the damage region must be exactly that child's rectangle expressed in the shared target coordinate system
repaint a widget inside the separate top-level dialog; it must be excluded from the shared target damage even though the dialog's parent widget is the target

observations: QWidget::grab() and QWidget::render() must be called on the GUI thread. Both are implemented by repainting the widget through QWidget::render(), so the call is synchronous and blocks the GUI thread for its duration.
Neither call needs a current OpenGL context for raster widgets. A QWidget hierarchy that contains a QOpenGLWidget/D3D child is the case that needs a graphics context (see the openglwidget sample).

Popups, QMenu and non-modal QDialog are separate top-level windows and are NOT part of a top-level widget capture. The target adapter must decide whether to share only the main window or to compose extra windows.

Damage regions must be mapped into the shared target coordinate system before they are unioned. Child widgets report QPaintEvent::region() in their own coordinate system, so the tracker binds the top-level window widget as the shared target, translates each accepted child region with QWidget::mapTo() and clips it to the visible part of the ancestor chain.

Storage identity (real backing-store address from QImage::constBits(), not QImage::cacheKey()): the reused producer target changed its pixel storage in 6 of 75 captures, and the address never moved on its own between captures (0 self-check hits). QImage uses implicit data sharing: QImage::detach() copies when the reference count is not 1, so a producer that published a shared QImage pays for a new allocation exactly on the captures where a consumer still held the previous frame. This is a copy-on-write semantic, not a fixed per-frame allocation rate: with no consumer holding a frame the same buffer is reused with no replacement at all.

Storage-identity probe controls: the synthetic shared-write control relocated the storage in 75 of 75 runs (probe can detect a replacement), and the unique-write control kept the same address in 75 of 75 runs (the probe does not report phantom replacements).
Storage-identity probe (real backing-store address from QImage::constBits(), not QImage::cacheKey()): 'QWidget::render() into reused QImage' probed 60 captures and replaced its pixel storage 6 times.

Damage probe (mapped into the shared target coordinate system): 2640 paint events from the target subtree were accepted, 0 paint events were excluded because they belong to separate top-level windows or non-widget objects, and 0 mapped events fell outside the target rect. Application repaints covered 83.5 % of the shared target rect per frame on average, while the capture calls added 100.0 %. This is an observable child-region stream after mapping and clipping; it is not yet a transport-ready damage protocol.

notes: grabs the widget through QWidget::render(); includes child widgets, excludes popups and dialogs that are separate top-level windows; triggers real paint events

draws directly into a caller-owned QImage that is reused for every capture; the measured time covers the buffer clear and the render, and the pixel storage address is probed with QImage::constBits() before the clear and after the render

same public API as the reused variant, but the target image is allocated and cleared for every capture; the measured time covers the allocation, the clear and the render, so it is directly comparable with the reused variant

paints into a caller-owned raw pixel buffer and only publishes a borrowed view of that memory; this is the shape a zero-copy (GBM/DMA-BUF) producer would take. The measured time therefore excludes the one deep copy the harness performs for reporting

observations: QQuickWidget::grabFramebuffer() returns the Quick render target, so the result excludes the surrounding raster widgets and has the Quick item size, not the window size.
Full-parent QWidget::grab() composes the embedded Quick content and the raster siblings into one image, which is the simpler contract for a whole-window target.

Input coordinates differ between the two paths: a viewer coordinate must be translated from the parent widget geometry into the QQuickWidget's own coordinate space before it is delivered to the embedded Quick item.
QQuickWidget owns an offscreen render target and its own render loop, so capture cost includes one extra composition/readback step compared with a native QQuickWindow.

Damage probe (mapped into the shared target coordinate system): 509 paint events from the target subtree were accepted, 0 paint events were excluded because they belong to separate top-level windows or non-widget objects, and 0 mapped events fell outside the target rect. Application repaints covered 86.3 % of the shared target rect per frame on average, while the capture calls added 100.0 %. This is an observable child-region stream after mapping and clipping; it is not yet a transport-ready damage protocol.

notes: Quick-specific capture: returns the Quick content only, at the Quick render target size. It does not include the raster siblings of the parent widget
full-parent capture: includes the embedded Quick content and every raster sibling, which is what a whole-window sharing target needs
